core_obligations: Choose a surjection A[x_1, ..., x_n] to B and a presentation matrix (h_ij) for M over that polynomial ring (proof lines 21109-21113).
Choose a presentation A = R[y_1, ..., y_m]/(g_1, ..., g_u) and lift the entries h_ij to polynomials h'_ij over R in all the variables (proof lines 21114-21118).
Display the presentation of M over R[y_1, ..., y_m, x_1, ..., x_n] whose matrix is the block matrix with first block (h'_ij) and u further blocks g_i times the identity (proof lines 21119-21125).
Conclude that M is finitely presented relative to R (proof lines 21126-21128).

difficulty_reason: The lemma is the transitivity statement for the relative notion of finite presentation: for finite type maps R to A to B, a B-module M that is finitely presented relative to A is finitely presented relative to R as soon as A is of finite presentation over R (statement lines 21101-21105). The proof is a 21-line explicit presentation (proof lines 21108-21128) which chooses a presentation of B over A[x_1, ..., x_n], a presentation matrix for M over that polynomial ring, and a presentation of A over R[y_1, ..., y_m], lifts the entries of the matrix to the polynomial ring over R in both sets of variables, and then writes a presentation matrix whose first block is the lifted matrix and whose remaining blocks are the equations of A multiplied by the identity. As in the base change statement of the same block, the work is the construction of the matrix and the claim that it presents M over a polynomial ring over R; the author states both without verifying the block computation.
